title: Compact pebbles and the evolution of volatiles in the interstellar comet 2I/Borisov
question: Characterize the dust particle properties (size, porosity, mass loss rate) and pre-perihelion CO gas production in the interstellar comet 2I/Borisov to understand its formation and volatile evolution.

recipe.goal: Measure multi-band ALMA dust continuum flux and noise
recipe.method: Convolve all four continuum images with a fixed resolution element of 3.4" x 2.3", integrate total flux within one FWHM of the resolution element at the image center, and estimate RMS by averaging RMS measurements within one beam at multiple locations near the center.
assumptions: Nucleus thermal contribution is negligible (at most 3.73, 1.65, 0.64, and 0.36 uJy in Bands 7, 6, 4, 3 for r_n <= 0.4 km and Bond albedo 0.04)

recipe.goal: Model dust thermal SED and derive dust particle size, porosity, mass, and mass loss rate
recipe.method: Use Mie theory combined with Bruggeman effective medium theory to compute absorption cross sections C_abs(a, lambda), solve radiative equilibrium for grain temperature T(a, r_h), compute model flux density for single-sized grains and Divine-type size distributions, and derive mass loss rate from beam crossing time.
key_parameters: Divine-type distribution: alpha = 3.5, a_min = 1 um, a_max = 1 cm, peak a_p = 1 mm (area-weighted peak a_p' = 2.3 mm)
assumptions: Spherical grains; mass mixing ratio m_carb/m_sil = 0.5; compact dust density rho_CD = 2650 kg m^-3 (or porous P = 0.80 with rho_CD = 530 kg m^-3); dust velocity v_d = 3 m s^-1; nucleus bulk density = 500 kg m^-3 and radius r_n = 0.4 km.

recipe.goal: Extract and model CO J=3-2 and J=2-1 emission to derive CO production rate, temperature, and CO/H2O ratio
recipe.method: Extract CO spectra from emission peak positions, model simultaneously with a spherically symmetric LTE coma radiative transfer model subject to solar photolysis, account for interferometric spatial filtering via CASA simobserve, and combine with literature H2O production rate.
key_parameters: Same hour angle, observation duration, and C43-2 array configuration in simobserve
assumptions: Spherically symmetric coma in LTE expanding at constant outflow velocity of 0.47 km s^-1; H2O production rate Q(H2O) = (10.7 +/- 1.2) x 10^26 s^-1

recipe.goal: Measure optical coma reflectivity slope, Af rho, and optical dust mass loss rates from VLT/FORS2
recipe.method: Process FORS2 images in ESO MIDAS, calibrate photometry against Pan-STARRS and SDSS stars, measure magnitudes in a 5" radius circular aperture, convert R magnitudes to Af rho, and compute order-of-magnitude Q(dust).
assumptions: rho_d = 2650 kg m^-3, v_d = 3 m s^-1, mean dust size <a> = 1 mm, geometrical albedo p_V = 0.04
